questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully:

(1) Cinnamon is a spice obtained from the inner bark of several tree species from the genus Cinnamomum. Cinnamon is made by cutting the stems of cinnamon trees. The inner bark is then extracted and the woody parts removed. When it dries, it forms strips that curl into rolls, called cinnamon sticks. These sticks can be ground to form cinnamon powder. The spice, consisting of the dried inner bark, is brown in colour and has a delicately fragrant aroma and a warm sweet flavour. The distinct aroma and flavour of cinnamon derive from its essential oil and principal component, cinnamaldehyde, as well as numerous other constituents including eugenol.

(2) There are two main types of cinnamon: Cassia and Ceylon. The two have different nutritional profiles. Ceylon cinnamon comes from Sri Lanka. Some people call it "true cinnamon." Cassia cinnamon, on the other hand, originates from southern China. Cassia is cheaper than Ceylon cinnamon. Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, somewhat bitter flavour while Ceylon is sweeter and lighter in flavor.

(3) Cinnamon was once more valuable than gold. In Egypt it was sought for embalming and religious practices. In medieval Europe it was used for religious rites and as a flavouring agent. Later it was the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade.

(4) Cinnamon is widely used as an aromatic condiment and flavouring additive in a wide variety of cuisines, sweet and savoury dishes, breakfast cereals, snack foods, bagels, teas, hot chocolate and traditional foods.

(5) Cinnamon is a spice that has been prized for its medicinal properties for thousands of years. In recent years, modern science has started to confirm many of the potential health benefits associated with cinnamon. Cinnamon has antimicrobial and antifungal properties, which is why it's often found in dental-hygiene products and is sold as cinnamon supplements. It is also a good source of antioxidants, substances that inhibit the effect of free radicals (reactive atoms that can damage cells). Due to its anti-inflammatory nature, cinnamon is currently being researched for its potential to fight Alzheimer's disease and decrease symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer.

(6) Studies also suggest that cinnamon has anti-diabetic properties, and may offer protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease, among other conditions. However, more evidence is needed to confirm cinnamon's benefits. In the short term, consuming moderate amounts of cinnamon as a spice or as a supplement seems to be safe for most people. However, cinnamon contains coumarin. This is a natural flavouring, but it also plays a role in creating warfarin, the common blood-thinning drug. Consuming too much coumarin can lead to liver damage and affect coagulation.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The characteristic aroma and flavour of cinnamon originate from its essential oil, primarily composed of ___________. [Paragraph (1)]
sub_questions.solution: According to Paragraph (1), the distinct aroma and flavour of cinnamon derive from its essential oil and principal component, cinnamaldehyde, along with other constituents including eugenol. Therefore, the characteristic aroma and flavour of cinnamon originate from its essential oil, primarily composed of cinnamaldehyde.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the reading of the passage, examine, in about 40 words, how cinnamon derived from the trees is made fit to be used as a spice. [Paragraph (1)]

key_points: The stems of cinnamon trees are cut.
The inner bark is extracted and woody parts are removed.
When dried, the bark forms strips that curl into rolls called cinnamon sticks, which can be ground into powder.

sub_questions.solution: To make cinnamon fit for use as a spice, the stems of cinnamon trees are first cut. The inner bark is then extracted and the woody parts are removed. As the bark dries, it forms strips that curl into rolls called cinnamon sticks. These sticks can then be ground into fine cinnamon powder.

sub_questions.text_english: Mention one point of difference between Ceylon cinnamon and Cassia cinnamon. [Paragraph (2)]

key_points: Ceylon cinnamon has a sweeter and lighter flavour, while Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, and somewhat bitter flavour.

sub_questions.solution: One key difference is in their flavour profiles. Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, and somewhat bitter flavour, whereas Ceylon cinnamon is sweeter and lighter in flavour. Additionally, Ceylon comes from Sri Lanka and is more expensive, while Cassia originates from southern China.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The author says that cinnamon was once more valuable than gold because ___________. [Paragraph (3)]

fill_values: it was highly sought after for embalming and religious practices in Egypt, for religious rites and as a flavouring agent in medieval Europe, and was the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade

sub_questions.solution: The author says that cinnamon was once more valuable than gold because it was highly sought after across civilisations — in Egypt for embalming and religious practices, in medieval Europe for religious rites and as a flavouring agent, and it was even the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the tone of the writer in the given lines from paragraph (5)? Rationalize your response in about 40 words. "Cinnamon is a spice that has been prized for its medicinal properties for thousands of years."

key_points: The tone is informative and appreciative.
The writer presents cinnamon's long history of medicinal use as a well-established fact.
The phrase 'thousands of years' emphasises the depth of trust humans have placed in this spice.

sub_questions.solution: The tone of the writer is informative and appreciative. By stating that cinnamon has been prized for thousands of years, the writer conveys a deep respect for the spice's historical significance. The phrase underscores how ancient civilisations consistently valued cinnamon for its healing properties, lending credibility and reverence to the discussion.

sub_questions.text_english: The writer's use of the phrases 'modern science has started to confirm' in paragraph (5) and 'more evidence is needed to confirm' in paragraph (6) suggests that the benefits of cinnamon are: 1. proven 2. scientific 3. uncertain 4. controversial 5. harmful. Select the correct option.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) only 3 — uncertain. The phrase 'modern science has started to confirm' implies the process is not yet complete, and 'more evidence is needed to confirm' directly signals that the benefits are not yet proven. This shows the benefits remain uncertain. Options A, B, and D are incorrect because the text does not label the benefits as proven, controversial, or harmful.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements about cinnamon and its health benefits is true?

options_english.A: Modern science has evidence to prove that cinnamon has many anti-diabetic properties, and it offers complete protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease.
options_english.B: Cinnamon lacks antimicrobial and antifungal properties, making it unsuitable for dental hygiene products.
options_english.C: Antioxidants found in cinnamon have no effect on free radicals in the body.
options_english.D: Cinnamon's anti-inflammatory properties are being researched for its potential benefits in Alzheimer's disease, irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Paragraph (5) clearly states that due to its anti-inflammatory nature, cinnamon is being researched for its potential to fight Alzheimer's disease and decrease symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer. Option A is wrong because science has only started to confirm benefits, not proven them fully. Option B is wrong because cinnamon does have antimicrobial and antifungal properties. Option C is wrong as antioxidants in cinnamon do inhibit free radicals.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements best describes the author's attitude toward cinnamon and its uses?

options_english.A: Finds cinnamon to be a prized condiment which can be used in almost all food items.
options_english.B: Believes that cinnamon should be used by everyone, everyday.
options_english.C: Recognizes that cinnamon has many useful properties, including health benefits.
options_english.D: Believes that cinnamon should only be used as a medicinal supplement.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Throughout the passage, the author presents cinnamon in a balanced and comprehensive manner — discussing its historical value, culinary uses, and medicinal properties. The author neither limits cinnamon to food use (ruling out A) nor recommends universal daily use (ruling out B) nor restricts it to medicinal supplements only (ruling out D). The overall attitude is one of recognising its wide-ranging useful properties.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully:

(1) When planning vacations, Indians typically prioritize domestic destinations, as shown by Ministry of Tourism data indicating 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits within India compared to 21 million international departures in 2022. Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka stand out as the top states for domestic tourism. Reasons for domestic tourism are many, some travel because it suits their budget while others love to explore the historical, cultural diversity. The government today is focussing on tourist-friendly infrastructure which is making travel more convenient for the domestic traveller.

(2) In terms of outbound tourism, a significant proportion of Indian travellers, totalling 5.9 million, visited the United Arab Emirates in 2022, comprising 28 percent of total outbound tourist travel. Other Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait also rank among the top destinations, with 2.4 million, 880,000, and 830,000 Indian visitors, respectively. Additionally, countries like the United States and the United Kingdom attract a considerable number of Indian tourists because these countries offer a mix of traditional and contemporary experiences along with enjoying unique cuisines and diverse landscapes.

(3) The popularity of Gulf States and the U.S. may be influenced by migration trends. The current issue of the International Organization for Migration's (IOM) World Migration Report highlights significant migration flows from India to the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and Saudi Arabia. For instance, the Emirates hosted approximately 3.6 million Indian migrants as of August 2023. Only via two corridors have more people transferred from one country to another as of 2020 according to the IOM: Mexico to the United States with around 11 million and Syria to Turkey with approximately 4 million. These migration corridors rank among the top ten globally.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: What does the use of the phrase 'prioritise domestic destinations' by the writer, in paragraph (1) imply?

options_english.A: Indian tourists prefer places in the country itself.
options_english.B: Indian tourists like to stay at home.
options_english.C: Indian tourists mainly travel on low budgets.
options_english.D: Indian tourists love to hitch-hike and trek.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The phrase 'prioritise domestic destinations' means that Indians give first preference to travel spots within their own country rather than abroad. This is clearly supported by the data showing 1.7 billion domestic visits compared to only 21 million international departures. Option B is wrong as travelling domestically is not the same as staying home. Options C and D are too specific and not implied by the phrase.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate option from those given in brackets, based on your understanding of paragraph (2). The statement that, World Migration Report highlights significant migration flows from India to the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and Saudi Arabia, is a/an ________ (fact/opinion) because it is a/an __________ (subjective judgement/objective detail).
sub_questions.solution: The statement is a fact because it is an objective detail. It is based on data published by the International Organization for Migration's World Migration Report, which is a credible and measurable source. A fact can be verified, and since this is drawn from an official report with quantifiable data, it is objective rather than a subjective judgement or personal opinion.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw a comparative analysis of domestic tourists travelling within India with domestic tourists travelling outside India in 2022. Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: In 2022, domestic tourist visits within India totalled 1.7 billion.
International departures were only 21 million.
Domestic travel far outweighed outbound travel, indicating strong preference for travel within the country.

sub_questions.solution: In 2022, domestic tourist visits within India were significantly higher at 1.7 billion, compared to only 21 million international departures. This stark contrast reveals that the vast majority of Indian tourists prefer travelling within the country, likely due to affordability, cultural connection, and improved domestic infrastructure.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following with a suitable reason. Gulf states rank as popular destinations for Indians _________.

fill_values: because of significant migration flows from India to these regions, as many Indians have family and community ties in the Gulf countries, particularly the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait

sub_questions.solution: Gulf states rank as popular destinations for Indians because of significant migration flows from India to these regions. The UAE hosted approximately 3.6 million Indian migrants as of August 2023, and the India-UAE migration corridor ranks among the top ten globally. Indians visiting these destinations are often reuniting with family or community members settled there.

sub_questions.text_english: Select the option that is true for the Assertion and Reason given below. Assertion: Indians prioritize Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh for domestic tourism. Reason: These states are full of historical monuments.

options_english.A: Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.B: Both the Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.C: The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
options_english.D: The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). The assertion is true — Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh are indeed among the top five states for domestic tourism as mentioned in paragraph (1). The reason is also broadly true as these states are home to historical monuments. However, the passage states that people travel for various reasons including budget and cultural diversity, not solely because of historical monuments, so the reason is not the correct or complete explanation of the assertion.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The fourthmost visited outbound destination for Indians to the Gulf is _________.
sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph (2), among Gulf states, the UAE was the most visited with 5.9 million Indians, followed by Saudi Arabia with 2.4 million, then Qatar with 880,000 visitors, and Kuwait with 830,000 visitors. Therefore, Kuwait is the fourth most visited outbound Gulf destination for Indian tourists.

sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two reasons for domestic tourism becoming popular.

key_points: Budget-friendly travel
Desire to explore historical and cultural diversity of India

sub_questions.solution: Two reasons for the growing popularity of domestic tourism are: first, it suits the budget of many Indian travellers as it is more affordable than international travel; and second, people are motivated by a desire to explore India's rich historical and cultural diversity. Additionally, the government's focus on tourist-friendly infrastructure has made domestic travel more convenient.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the writer's view about the tourism industry in the west? Write any two points.

key_points: Western countries like the US and UK attract Indian tourists.
They offer a mix of traditional and contemporary experiences, unique cuisines, and diverse landscapes.

sub_questions.solution: According to the writer, western countries like the United States and the United Kingdom attract a considerable number of Indian tourists. Two reasons for this are: first, these countries offer a rich mix of traditional and contemporary experiences; and second, they provide opportunities to enjoy unique cuisines and explore diverse landscapes, making them appealing destinations.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the word in paragraph (3) that indicates the 'preference' of people travelling to the Gulf.

key_points: popularity

sub_questions.solution: The word in paragraph (3) that indicates the preference of people travelling to the Gulf is 'popularity'. The paragraph begins by stating that the popularity of Gulf States and the U.S. may be influenced by migration trends, which clearly reflects the preference and attraction that Indian travellers have towards these destinations.

questions.text_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed.
questions.instruction_line_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed.
questions.solution: Grammar task set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the brackets, for the given portion of a letter. I believe that with your support and ________ (cooperate), we can find a mutually agreeable solution that meets the expectations of all stakeholders involved.
sub_questions.solution: The blank requires a noun form of the verb 'cooperate' because it follows the conjunction 'and' and is parallel to the noun 'support'. The correct noun form is 'cooperation'. The complete sentence reads: I believe that with your support and cooperation, we can find a mutually agreeable solution that meets the expectations of all stakeholders involved.

sub_questions.text_english: Read the given sentence from an electric cooker's instruction manual. Identify the error and supply the correction in the sentence. For avoid damaging the appliance, do not immerse the electric cooker in water or any other liquid.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the use of the base verb 'avoid' after the preposition 'for'. In English, a preposition must be followed by a gerund (verb+ing form), not a base verb. Therefore, 'avoid' should be corrected to 'avoiding'. The correct sentence reads: For avoiding damaging the appliance, do not immerse the electric cooker in water or any other liquid.

sub_questions.text_english: Amit and Pallavi had a conversation about the inauguration of Pallavi's event. Report Amit's question. Did you manage to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the next month?

key_points: Amit asked Pallavi if she had managed to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the following month.

sub_questions.solution: In reported speech, the question word 'did' is removed and the auxiliary shifts to 'had'. 'You' changes to 'she' and 'next' changes to 'following'. Amit asked Pallavi if she had managed to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the following month.

sub_questions.text_english: Read the dialogue between Bharti and her mother, Geeta, regarding Geeta's birthday plans. Bharti: Do you want to go to a hill station on your birthday? Geeta: No, I want to stay at home and call my friends over. Select the correct option that reports the above dialogue. Bharti asked Geeta if she wanted to go to a hill station on her birthday. Geeta replied in the negative and said that __________.

options_english.A: she wanted to stay home and call her friends for celebrating.
options_english.B: I wanted to stay home and call my friends to celebrate.
options_english.C: she wanted to stay at home and call her friends over.
options_english.D: she wants to stay home by calling her friends to celebrate.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). In reported speech, the first person pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' (referring to Geeta), and the present tense 'want' changes to past tense 'wanted'. The original phrasing 'call my friends over' becomes 'call her friends over', preserving the original meaning. Option A adds unnecessary meaning, Option B incorrectly retains the first person, and Option D uses the wrong tense 'wants'.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete the line of a notice placed on the notice board of a company. Please be informed that there will be a staff meeting in the conference room on Friday, 7th June, at 10:00 a.m. It is __________ for all to attend. (mandatory/obligatory/indispensable)
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'mandatory'. In formal notices and official communications, 'mandatory' is the standard word used to mean required by authority or rule. While 'obligatory' can also mean required, 'mandatory' is the most appropriate and commonly used term in official notices. 'Indispensable' means absolutely necessary and is not typically used in this context. The complete sentence reads: It is mandatory for all to attend.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the error and supply correction for the given sentence from a preface of a book. Writing this book have been a journey of exploration and discovery.
sub_questions.solution: The error is 'have' which should be corrected to 'has'. The subject of the sentence is the gerund phrase 'Writing this book', which acts as a singular noun and therefore takes the singular verb 'has' rather than the plural 'have'. The correct sentence reads: Writing this book has been a journey of exploration and discovery.

sub_questions.text_english: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line, from an analytical paragraph. The advent of social media has revolutionized communication by connected people across the globe in unprecedented ways.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The error is 'connected', which should be 'connecting'. After the preposition 'by', a gerund (verb+ing) form is required. 'Connected' is a past participle and is grammatically incorrect in this position. Option A is wrong because the subject 'advent' is singular and 'has' is correct. Option B incorrectly changes 'communication' to 'communicating'. Option D is wrong as 'in' is correct in context.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the given entry in a personal diary, by filling the blank with the correct option. Today was a rollercoaster of emotions. It started off with a sense of excitement and anticipation as I __________ on a new project at work.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) embarked. The diary entry describes past events ('Today was', 'It started off'), so the verb in the blank must be in the simple past tense. 'Embarked' is the simple past form of 'embark' and correctly fits the context. Option A (embarking) is a present participle, Option B (embark) is a base form, and Option D (have embarked) is present perfect — all inconsistent with the past tense context of the diary entry.

sub_questions.text_english: Report the dialogue between a salesman and his customer, by completing the sentence. Salesman: I have a wide range of sportswear. Customer: Please show me something in cotton fabric, which is suitable for summers. The salesman stated ____________. The customer requested the salesman to show something in cotton fabric which would be suitable for summers.

fill_values: that he had a wide range of sportswear

sub_questions.solution: In reported speech, the first person pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' (referring to the salesman), and the present tense 'have' shifts to past tense 'had'. The complete sentence reads: The salesman stated that he had a wide range of sportswear. The customer requested the salesman to show something in cotton fabric which would be suitable for summers.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete an announcement on a flight. In thirty minutes, our flight attendants ________ meal service.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) will begin. The sentence refers to a future action that is certain to happen ('In thirty minutes'), so the simple future tense 'will begin' is appropriate. Option A is grammatically incorrect as 'will' must be followed by the base verb 'begin', not the past tense 'began'. Options C and D ('should begin' and 'can begin') express possibility or ability, not a definite scheduled future action.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the line from a 'Save the Environment' song, by filling the blank with the correct option. Pollution, pollution, its time to take a stand, for the health of our planet, we've got to lend a hand, Reduce, reuse, recycle, that's the key, ________ our world for you and me.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) to preserve. In English, an infinitive of purpose is formed with 'to' followed by the base form of the verb. The line expresses the purpose of reducing, reusing, and recycling, which is 'to preserve' the world. Option A is wrong because 'for' is followed by a noun or gerund, not a base verb. Options C and D use 'preserved' which is a past participle and grammatically incorrect in this structure.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the error and supply the correction for the following instruction put up for safe use of elevators. Please refrain by standing near the door as it could lead to an accident.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the preposition 'by', which should be corrected to 'from'. The verb 'refrain' is always followed by the preposition 'from', not 'by'. This is a standard collocation in English. The correct sentence reads: Please refrain from standing near the door as it could lead to an accident.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below.
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below.
questions.solution: Letter writing task. Model answers are provided in sub_questions for both options.

sub_questions.text_english: As Sakshi/Saksham Bedi of 864, Solar Apartments, Lajpat Street, Dipak Nagar, you feel that the lack of proper street lighting in several areas of your neighbourhood is a threat to safety. Residents, especially those who work late shifts or return home after dark, feel vulnerable due to poorly lit streets. Write a letter to the District Magistrate of your city area, in about 120 words, stating the problem and requesting him to take necessary action for installation of streetlights in those areas.

key_points: Proper format: sender's address, date, recipient's designation and address, subject line
Opening: purpose of writing — lack of street lighting
Body: impact on residents, especially those returning after dark
Request: urgent installation of streetlights
Closing: polite request for action

sub_questions.solution:
864, Solar Apartments,
Lajpat Street, Dipak Nagar
[Date]

The District Magistrate,
[City Name]

Subject: Request for Installation of Streetlights in Dipak Nagar

Respected Sir/Madam,

I am writing to bring to your kind attention the serious problem of inadequate street lighting in several areas of Dipak Nagar. The poorly lit streets pose a significant safety threat to residents, particularly those who work night shifts or return home after dark. The darkness makes them vulnerable to accidents and criminal activities.

Despite repeated complaints to local authorities, no action has been taken so far. I earnestly request you to kindly direct the concerned department to install adequate streetlights in these areas at the earliest.

Your prompt action will be greatly appreciated by all residents.

Yours faithfully,
Sakshi/Saksham Bedi

sub_questions.text_english: You are Dharti Pradhan/Balal Goyal, the head girl/boy of Pinnacle School, Ustahpuri. You live in a culturally rich city with many historical monuments. You have observed that visitors have etched graffiti on these monuments and littered the area around. You are extremely disturbed at this irresponsible behaviour of the visitors. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, in about 120 words, suggesting measures to stop such vandalism and creating awareness about the importance of these monuments.

key_points: Proper letter-to-editor format with address, date, subject
Opening: reason for writing — vandalism of historical monuments
Body: problem description and suggested measures
Call to action: awareness and stricter enforcement
Closing: polite and concerned tone

sub_questions.solution:
Pinnacle School,
Ustahpuri
[Date]

The Editor,
[Name of National Daily]

Subject: Vandalism of Historical Monuments — A Growing Concern

Dear Editor,

Through the esteemed columns of your newspaper, I wish to express my deep concern over the increasing vandalism of historical monuments in our city. Visitors have been etching graffiti on these priceless structures and littering the surrounding areas, causing irreversible damage to our cultural heritage.

I urge the authorities to install surveillance cameras, impose heavy fines on offenders, and deploy more security personnel at these sites. Schools and colleges must conduct awareness drives emphasising the importance of preserving our heritage. Media campaigns can also play a vital role in educating the public.

I hope this issue receives urgent attention.

Yours sincerely,
Dharti Pradhan/Balal Goyal

questions.text_english: Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below.
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below.
questions.solution: Analytical paragraph task. Model answers are provided in sub_questions for both options.

sub_questions.text_english: Natural food, typically refers to food that has not been processed or preserved in any significant way before it is consumed, while ultra-processed food refers to food items that have been altered from their natural state through various methods. Study the description given and write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, drawing a comparison between the two based on the table provided.

key_points: Introduce the two types of food
Compare fibre, nutrients, and fats
Compare sodium content
Discuss health outcomes of each
Conclude with a recommendation

sub_questions.solution: Natural and processed foods differ significantly in their nutritional value and impact on health. Natural foods are high in fibre, healthy nutrients, and healthy fats, while having low sodium levels. This makes them ideal for regulating blood sugar, controlling blood pressure, and providing the body with essential nourishment. In contrast, processed foods are high in sugar, unhealthy nutrients, unhealthy fats, and sodium, which can lead to lifestyle diseases. Their only apparent advantage is that they are tasty, ready to eat, and convenient, which makes them addictive. While processed food appeals to modern, fast-paced lifestyles, it poses serious health risks in the long run. Therefore, a conscious shift towards natural, wholesome food is essential for maintaining good health and overall well-being.

sub_questions.text_english: Social Media has a lasting impact on our thought process and influences our thinking in both positive and negative ways. With the help of the given cues and using your own ideas, write an analytical paragraph on 'The Impact of Social Media on Teenagers' in about 120 words. POSITIVE: connects peers, creative expression, access information, community building. NEGATIVE: impacts self-esteem, cyber bullying, privacy intrusion, distraction and addiction.

key_points: Introduce social media's role in teenagers' lives
Discuss positive impacts: connectivity, creativity, information access
Discuss negative impacts: self-esteem, cyberbullying, addiction
Balanced conclusion

sub_questions.solution: Social media has become an integral part of teenage life, shaping their thoughts, relationships, and sense of identity in both positive and negative ways. On the positive side, it helps teenagers connect with peers, form communities of shared interest, and express themselves creatively through art, writing, and videos. It also provides easy access to information and educational resources. However, the negative consequences are equally significant. Constant comparison with curated online images can damage self-esteem. Cyberbullying has emerged as a serious threat to mental health. Privacy intrusion and data misuse are growing concerns. Moreover, excessive use leads to distraction from studies and addiction. Therefore, teenagers must be guided to use social media responsibly, balancing its benefits while being aware of its potential harms.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.solution: Extract-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (a): 'He felt certain that his wings would never support him; so he bent his head and ran away back to the little hole under the ledge where he slept at night. Even when each of his brothers and his little sister, whose wings were far shorter than his own, ran to the brink, flapped their wings, and flew away, he failed to muster up courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate. His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away. But for the life of him he could not move.' (Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight).

State any one inference about the parents of the baby seagull from the given statement: 'His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away.'

key_points: The parents were deeply concerned about the baby seagull's development and were using tough love to push him into flying.

sub_questions.solution: One inference is that the parents of the baby seagull were deeply concerned about his growth and used strict, tough-love tactics to motivate him. By threatening to let him starve and scolding him loudly, they were not being cruel but rather urging him to overcome his fear and take the essential step of learning to fly.

sub_questions.text_english: Where did the little seagull sleep at night? [Extract (a) – His First Flight]

key_points: The little seagull slept at night in a little hole under the ledge.

sub_questions.solution: According to the extract from 'His First Flight', the little seagull slept at night in a little hole under the ledge. When he was too afraid to fly, he bent his head and ran back to this familiar hiding spot, which served as his safe refuge.

sub_questions.text_english: Which factors contributed to the young seagull's reluctance to fly despite the encouragement and threats from his parents? Elaborate in about 40 words, with reference to the extract. [His First Flight]

key_points: The young seagull was convinced his wings would not support him.
The idea of taking the plunge seemed desperate and terrifying.
Even seeing his siblings with shorter wings fly away did not boost his confidence.

sub_questions.solution: The young seagull's reluctance stemmed from his deep self-doubt. He was convinced his wings could never support him in flight. The thought of jumping off the ledge seemed desperately dangerous. Even watching his siblings, who had shorter wings, fly away successfully could not overcome his paralysing fear of failure.

sub_questions.text_english: Which phrase or word would correctly substitute 'muster up' in the given sentence from the extract? He failed to 'muster up' courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate. [His First Flight]
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) gather. 'Muster up' means to summon or collect something, particularly an inner quality like courage. 'Gather' is the closest synonym as it also means to collect or summon. 'Review' means to examine, 'resolve' means to decide firmly, and 'distribute' means to spread out — none of these capture the meaning of summoning inner courage as accurately as 'gather'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (b): 'Tricki was tottering along in his little tweed coat.... He struggled on, drooping in his harness. I thought it wouldn't be long before I heard from Mrs. Pumphrey. The expected call came within a few days. Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught. Tricki would eat nothing. Refused even his favourite dishes; and besides, he had bouts of vomiting. He spent all his time lying on a rug, panting. Didn't want to go for walks, didn't want to do anything. I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalized for about a fortnight to be kept under observation. The poor lady almost swooned. She was sure he would pine and die if he did not see her every day. But I took a firm line. Tricki was very ill and this was the only way to save him.' (A Triumph of Surgery).

 Why had the author made his plans in advance?

options_english.A: Mrs. Pumphrey was worried that Tricki would pine and die without her.
options_english.B: The author was aware of the severity of Tricki's medical condition.
options_english.C: The author knew about Mrs. Pumphrey's financial condition.
options_english.D: The author had planned his own vacation.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). The author (the veterinarian) had already observed Tricki's deteriorating condition — he was tottering, drooping, and visibly unwell. Being a professional, he correctly anticipated that Tricki's condition would worsen and that Mrs. Pumphrey would soon call. Option A refers to Mrs. Pumphrey's fear, not the author's reason. Options C and D have no basis in the passage.

sub_questions.text_english: The author firmly proposed the need to remove Tricki from the house for a specified period. Elaborate the reason for doing so in about 40 words. [A Triumph of Surgery]

key_points: Tricki was severely ill — he was not eating, had bouts of vomiting, and was lethargic.
The author believed the home environment, likely full of overfeeding and pampering by Mrs. Pumphrey, was the root cause.
Hospitalisation for a fortnight was necessary for recovery.

sub_questions.solution: The author proposed removing Tricki from the house because the dog was critically ill. He had lost his appetite, suffered from vomiting, and lay listless on a rug all day. The author believed Mrs. Pumphrey's excessive pampering and overfeeding were the root causes, and only a disciplined hospital environment could help Tricki recover.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank with the correct word from the brackets. The word 'swooned' in the following sentence indicates almost ________ (tripped/fainted). [A Triumph of Surgery]
sub_questions.solution: The word 'swooned' means to faint or lose consciousness, typically due to extreme shock or distress. In this context, Mrs. Pumphrey almost swooned when she heard that Tricki needed to be hospitalised, indicating she was so overwhelmed with shock and worry that she nearly fainted. 'Tripped' means to stumble and does not carry this meaning.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught.' What does this suggest about her character? Mention any one reason. [A Triumph of Surgery]

key_points: Mrs. Pumphrey was deeply attached to Tricki and treated him like a family member, showing excessive emotional dependence on her pet.

sub_questions.solution: The statement 'Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught' suggests that she was excessively and emotionally attached to Tricki. She treated him not merely as a pet but as a beloved family member. Her extreme distress upon hearing that Tricki would not eat reveals her over-protective, indulgent nature, which was ironically the very cause of Tricki's illness.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.solution: Poetry extract-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (a): 'Some say the world will end in fire / Some say in ice. / From what I've tasted of desire / I hold with those who favour fire.' (Fire and Ice).

 The speaker offers evidence to support his preference for one theory over the other. Mention the evidence.

key_points: The speaker's personal experience of desire — a burning, consuming emotion — is the evidence he offers to support the theory that fire will end the world.

sub_questions.solution: In the poem 'Fire and Ice' by Robert Frost, the speaker uses his personal experience of desire as evidence to favour the fire theory. He says 'From what I've tasted of desire', meaning that desire, like fire, is a consuming and destructive force. This lived experience convinces him that the world is more likely to end in fire.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the prediction of the poet about how the world will come to an end? Answer in about 40 words. [Fire and Ice]

key_points: The poet believes fire (desire) will cause the end of the world.
However, he also acknowledges that ice (hatred) is equally powerful and capable of destroying the world.
Both human emotions — passion and hatred — are portrayed as destructive forces.

sub_questions.solution: Robert Frost predicts that the world will most likely end in fire, symbolising human desire and passion. However, he also acknowledges that if the world had to end twice, ice — representing hatred and indifference — would suffice. Both fire and ice, as symbols of destructive human emotions, are equally capable of bringing about the world's end.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Fire' and 'Ice' are used in the poem as _______. [Fire and Ice]
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) metaphors. 'Fire' and 'Ice' are used as metaphors — fire represents desire and passion, while ice represents hatred and indifference. A metaphor is a direct comparison without using 'like' or 'as'. They are not similes (A) as no comparison word is used. They are not oxymorons (D) as the two are not contradictory qualities in the same phrase, nor are they examples of repetition (C).

sub_questions.text_english: Comment on the overall mood of the extract. [Fire and Ice]

key_points: The overall mood is contemplative, dark, and resigned — the speaker calmly reflects on the destructive capacity of human nature without alarm.

sub_questions.solution: The overall mood of the extract is contemplative and darkly resigned. The poet reflects calmly on the possibility of the world's destruction, drawing upon his own experience of desire. Despite the grave subject matter, the tone is matter-of-fact and almost detached, suggesting a quiet acceptance of humanity's destructive impulses rather than dramatic alarm.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (b): 'The leaves strain toward the glass / small twigs stiff with exertion / long-cramped boughs shuffling under the roof / like newly discharged patients / half-dazed, moving / to the clinic doors.' (The Trees). 

How does the comparison between the boughs and newly discharged patients contribute to the theme or message of the poem? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: The comparison highlights the trees' slow, laboured movement towards freedom.
It reinforces the theme of nature reclaiming its space from human confinement.
The image of half-dazed patients suggests nature has been weakened by being confined indoors.

sub_questions.solution: The comparison between the boughs and newly discharged patients reinforces the poem's central theme of nature breaking free from confinement. Just as patients emerge from hospital weakened yet determined, the boughs shuffle slowly but purposefully towards freedom. This simile emphasises that nature, though restrained by humans, persistently strives to reclaim its rightful place in the open world.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence with the appropriate option. The imagery and descriptions in the poem create a mood of ______________________. [The Trees]
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) transition and uncertainty. The poem describes trees in the process of slowly moving from indoors to the outside — a state of being between confinement and freedom. The imagery of stiff twigs, shuffling boughs, and half-dazed patients all suggest a gradual, uncertain movement. Option A is too positive, Option C implies disorder, and Option D is contradictory — all are less accurate than (B).

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank with one word. The stiff movement of the twigs in the above extract suggests the ______________. [The Trees]
sub_questions.solution: The stiff movement of the twigs, described as 'stiff with exertion', suggests the struggle of the trees as they try to push their way out of the confined indoor space. The use of 'exertion' indicates that this movement requires great effort, pointing to the difficulty and strain experienced by nature in its attempt to break free.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the poet describe the bough as 'shuffling'? [The Trees]

key_points: The boughs are described as 'shuffling' because after being long-cramped indoors, they are moving slowly and awkwardly, much like a person who has been confined for too long and struggles to walk freely.

sub_questions.solution: The poet describes the boughs as 'shuffling' to convey their slow, constrained, and awkward movement. Having been long-cramped under the roof, the boughs lack the freedom and energy for graceful movement. The word 'shuffling' effectively captures the image of trees barely inching their way out, weighed down by the long period of confinement inside the house.

questions.text_english: Answer any four of the following five questions in 40 – 50 words each.

questions.solution: Short answer question set from literature. Answers provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: The transition from the apartheid system in South Africa to a new era of equality reflects broader historical trends in the struggle for human rights and social justice. Elaborate. (Nelson Mandela – Long Walk to Freedom)

key_points: Apartheid was a system of racial segregation that denied Black South Africans basic rights.
Mandela's inauguration marked the end of apartheid and the birth of a democratic, non-racial South Africa.
This transition echoes global struggles for civil rights and human dignity.

sub_questions.solution: The end of apartheid in South Africa, symbolised by Nelson Mandela's presidential inauguration, mirrors global struggles for justice and equality. Just as movements in America and India fought racial and colonial oppression, South Africa's transition demonstrated that sustained resistance can overcome systemic injustice. Mandela believed that oppressor and oppressed are both liberated when equality is achieved, reflecting a universal human rights principle.

sub_questions.text_english: How does 'The Ball Poem' by John Berryman explore the theme of loss and its profound impact on an individual's emotional state and perception of the world? (The Ball Poem)

key_points: The loss of the ball represents the boy's first experience of irreplaceable loss.
The poet uses the boy's grief to show how loss shapes one's understanding of responsibility and the impermanence of things.
The poem suggests that learning to cope with loss is a crucial part of growing up.

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Ball Poem', Berryman uses a boy's loss of his ball to explore the universal theme of loss. The ball, though a simple object, is irreplaceable in meaning to the boy. His grief is intense and real. The poet suggests that loss is a formative experience — it teaches individuals accountability, the impermanence of material possessions, and the emotional resilience needed to face life's inevitable disappointments.

sub_questions.text_english: How does the description of the baker's lifestyle in the past evoke a sense of nostalgia? (Glimpses of India – A Baker from Goa)

key_points: The baker's early morning visits with his bamboo staff and jingling sounds were a cherished part of Goan childhood.
The tradition of the Pader evokes memories of Portuguese-era Goa and simpler times.
The description of bread's role in festivals and celebrations reinforces cultural and emotional nostalgia.

sub_questions.solution: In 'A Baker from Goa', the description of the baker — or Pader — waking the village with the jingling of his bamboo staff and the aroma of fresh bread evokes a deep sense of nostalgia. These vivid childhood memories of a simpler, community-centred Goan life, rooted in Portuguese tradition, remind the narrator and reader of a warm, familiar past that modern life has gradually eroded.

sub_questions.text_english: What role does each of Belinda's pets play in the narrative? Select any two of her pets. (The Tale of Custard the Dragon)

key_points: Ink the cat and Blink the mouse (or Mustard the dog) act as boastful, brave characters who mock Custard for being a coward.
Custard the dragon appears cowardly but ultimately proves himself the bravest by defeating the pirate.
The contrast between appearance and reality is central to the poem.

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon', Mustard the dog and Ink the cat are portrayed as proud and boastful — they constantly mock Custard for being a coward. However, when a pirate threatens Belinda's household, it is Custard who bravely fights and defeats the intruder. The pets serve to highlight the poem's irony: those who boast the loudest prove the least brave in a true crisis.

sub_questions.text_english: Valli found joy and fascination in the simple act of watching the bus pass through her village. What does this reveal about her perspective on life and her surroundings? (Madam Rides the Bus)

key_points: Valli had a curious, adventurous spirit that found excitement in ordinary things.
The bus represented the outside world and freedom to her.
Her perspective reveals an imaginative and independent young mind longing to explore beyond her village.

sub_questions.solution: Valli's fascination with the bus reveals her curious, adventurous, and independent spirit. For her, the bus was not merely a vehicle but a gateway to the wider world beyond her small village. Her joy in watching it pass reflects an imaginative mind that finds wonder in the ordinary and harbours a deep longing to explore life beyond the boundaries of her limited daily existence.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Ausable get rid of Max? (The Midnight Visitor)

key_points: Ausable cleverly invented a story about a non-existent balcony below the window.
When a knock came at the door, Ausable said it was the police.
Max, fearing the police, stepped back onto the imaginary balcony and fell to his death.

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Midnight Visitor', Ausable cleverly outwitted Max through quick-witted deception. He fabricated a story about a balcony outside the window. When a knock came at the door, he told Max it was the police. Fearing arrest, Max stepped back expecting to find the balcony, but it did not exist. He fell and was thus eliminated without any physical confrontation.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does Mme Loisel hastily depart from the ball when her husband places a modest wrap on her shoulders? (The Necklace)

key_points: Mme Loisel is ashamed of her modest, ordinary wrap compared to the furs other women wore.
She feared that other elegantly dressed women would notice her poverty.
Her excessive vanity and insecurity about her social status drove her to flee quickly.

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Necklace', Mme Loisel departs hastily because she is deeply ashamed of the modest wrap her husband places on her shoulders. After a triumphant evening among the wealthy and elegantly dressed, she cannot bear the contrast between her borrowed jewellery and her ordinary coat. Her vanity and obsession with appearances make her flee before anyone notices her true social status.

sub_questions.text_english: 'In time you will be more learned than anyone else in the village. Then no one will ever be able to laugh at you.' What effect did her teacher's words have on Bholi? Elaborate. (Bholi)

key_points: The teacher's words gave Bholi hope and confidence for the first time in her life.
They motivated her to study hard and shed her inferiority complex.
Education transformed Bholi from a timid, underconfident girl into a bold and self-assured young woman.

sub_questions.solution: The teacher's encouraging words had a transformative effect on Bholi. For the first time, she felt valued and hopeful about her future. These words ignited a desire to learn and overcome her stammering and sense of inferiority. Education gradually built her confidence, ultimately transforming her from a timid, neglected girl into a bold and self-respecting woman who could stand up for herself.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 100 – 120 words.

questions.solution: Long answer question set. Model answers provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse and evaluate the role of faith in 'A Letter to God' and 'The Sermon at Benares'.

key_points: In 'A Letter to God', Lencho's unshakeable faith in God drives the entire narrative.
His faith is innocent and absolute — he believes God will help him after his crops are destroyed.
In 'The Sermon at Benares', the Buddha uses faith in the Dharma to guide Kisa Gotami through grief.
Both texts show faith as a source of strength, though Lencho's faith is naïve while the Buddha's teaching is wisdom-based.
Faith, in both cases, helps characters cope with loss and suffering.

sub_questions.solution: Faith plays a central and contrasting role in both 'A Letter to God' and 'The Sermon at Benares'. In 'A Letter to God', Lencho's faith in God is absolute and childlike. After a devastating hailstorm destroys his crops, he writes directly to God, firmly believing divine intervention will restore his livelihood. His faith never wavers even when the help comes through human hands. In 'The Sermon at Benares', the Buddha teaches Kisa Gotami, who is consumed by grief over her dead son, that death and suffering are universal. He guides her to accept this truth through the parable of the mustard seed, helping her find peace through wisdom and faith in the Dharma. While Lencho's faith is simple and literal, the Buddha's teaching channels faith into acceptance and understanding. Both texts affirm that faith — whether in God or in universal truth — is a profound source of strength that helps individuals endure hardship and loss.

sub_questions.text_english: Explore the contrasting images of the tiger in 'A Tiger in the Zoo' and the tiger in 'How to Tell Wild Animals'.

key_points: In 'A Tiger in the Zoo', the tiger is depicted as confined, restless, and robbed of its natural instincts.
The poem evokes sympathy for the captive tiger's loss of freedom.
In 'How to Tell Wild Animals', the tiger is described humorously as wild, powerful, and dangerous.
The tone in the second poem is light and comic, contrasting sharply with the sombre mood in the first.
Both poems together highlight the difference between natural freedom and imposed captivity.

sub_questions.solution: The two poems present sharply contrasting images of the tiger. In Leslie Norris's 'A Tiger in the Zoo', the tiger is a dignified but deeply unhappy captive. Confined in a concrete cell, it paces restlessly, its natural instincts suppressed. The poet evokes sympathy for the animal, highlighting the cruelty of captivity and humanity's failure to respect nature. The tiger gazes at the brilliant stars in silent, helpless longing — a powerful image of freedom denied. In contrast, Carolyn Wells's 'How to Tell Wild Animals' presents the tiger in a humorous, light-hearted tone. The wild tiger is described as fearsome and dangerous — it leaps upon you and leaves you in no doubt of its identity. The poem's comic treatment makes the tiger sound almost cartoonish, reducing its ferocity to a joke. Together, these two poems offer a complete picture — one mourning the loss of wildness, the other celebrating it through humour — reflecting two very different attitudes towards nature and wild animals.

sub_questions.text_english: Anil's acceptance and forgiveness of the thief demonstrates empathy and generosity. Elaborate. (The Thief's Story)

key_points: Anil knows that Hari Singh has stolen the money but chooses to forgive him.
He gives Hari a fifty rupee note the next morning, signalling acceptance.
Anil continues to teach Hari writing and cooking, showing genuine concern for his growth.
His forgiveness is not weakness but a deliberate act of empathy.
Anil's generosity transforms Hari, showing that compassion is more powerful than punishment.

sub_questions.solution: In Ruskin Bond's 'The Thief's Story', Anil's response to Hari Singh's theft is a remarkable demonstration of empathy and generosity. When Hari returns the stolen money after an internal moral struggle, Anil reveals that he was already aware of the theft but chooses not to confront or punish Hari. Instead, he hands him a fifty-rupee note the next morning, casually saying he had earned it. He also promises to pay him regularly and continues teaching him to read and write. Anil's forgiveness is not born of ignorance or weakness — it is a conscious, compassionate act. He understands that the young thief's dishonesty stems from poverty and lack of opportunity. By offering trust, education, and steady employment, Anil becomes a transformative force in Hari's life. His empathy silently challenges Hari to choose a better path. This quiet generosity ultimately proves more powerful than any punishment in prompting genuine moral change in the thief.

sub_questions.text_english: Trace the transformation of Richard Ebright from a young man with potential to a respected and accomplished scientist. (The Making of a Scientist)

key_points: Ebright began as a curious child who collected butterflies and earned a science fair prize.
His mother's support and a book on monarch butterflies sparked his scientific curiosity.
He conducted original research on viceroy butterflies and monarch gold spots.
His discovery of a new hormone in monarch butterflies was a milestone.
His passion for discovery, combined with competitive spirit and a good mind, led him to become a respected scientist.

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Making of a Scientist', Richard Ebright's transformation from a curious child into a respected scientist is a story of sustained passion, encouragement, and intellectual drive. As a young boy in Pennsylvania, Ebright began by collecting butterflies, coins, and fossils. His mother recognised his curiosity and nurtured it by providing books, including one about monarch butterflies that changed his life. Inspired by the book, Ebright began tagging monarch butterflies to study their migration patterns, earning recognition at science fairs. His curiosity deepened as he investigated the gold spots on monarch pupae, eventually discovering a hormone that plays a vital role in the butterfly's development. This groundbreaking research led him to later propose an important theory about cell communication. His competitive spirit, combined with a first-rate mind and genuine love for learning, allowed him to excel. Richard Ebright's journey illustrates that a great scientist is shaped not just by talent but by curiosity, encouragement, and the willingness to ask meaningful questions about the natural world.
